# [dv] Out of bounds access in dside access tracking logic

This line: https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/056cb44ff75f797898709546ea1b0fd08d862e1a/rtl/ibex_top.sv#L1092

Uses `i - 1` and it's possible to evaluate this condition when `i == 0` giving an out of bounds access. This logic needs refactoring to more explicitly split out the `i == 0` case from the others to ensure this does not occur.

## Phase 1: FIX ANALYSIS

### 1. Problem statement
The issue is an out-of-bounds array access in the data-side access tracking logic in `ibex_top.sv`.

In the `always_comb` block that updates `pending_dside_accesses_d[i]`, the code evaluates:

```systemverilog
pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid
```

when `i == 0` is possible. That means the design can attempt to read index `-1`, which is invalid and can cause simulation/synthesis issues or undefined behavior.

### 2. Where the problem occurs
The problematic code is in:

- `rtl/ibex_top.sv`
- inside the `for (genvar i = 0; i < MaxOutstandingDSideAccesses; i++) begin : g_dside_tracker`
- specifically in the `always_comb` block around the request-grant logic:

```systemverilog
if (data_req_o && data_gnt_i) begin
  if (i == 0 && !pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid) begin
    ...
  end else if (pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid &
               !pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid) begin
    ...
  end
end
```

Even though the `i == 0` case is handled first, the structure relies on conditional evaluation behavior in a way that is fragile and still flagged as an out-of-bounds risk. The fix should explicitly separate the `i == 0` case from all other cases.

### 3. Best practices to follow
- Avoid any expression that can index arrays with negative values, even if guarded by a condition.
- Explicitly separate boundary cases (`i == 0`) from general cases (`i > 0`).
- Keep the change minimal and localized to the affected logic.
- Preserve the existing behavior for all valid indices.
- Prefer clear, structurally safe control flow over relying on short-circuiting or nested conditions.

### 4. How to fix it
Refactor the `always_comb` block so that:

- when `i == 0`, only the `i == 0` logic is evaluated;
- for `i > 0`, the logic using `i - 1` is evaluated only in that branch.

A clean way is to wrap the request-grant update logic in:

```systemverilog
if (i == 0) begin
  ...
end else begin
  ...
end
```

This guarantees `i - 1` is never evaluated when `i == 0`.

## Phase 1: FIX ANALYSIS

### 1) What the problem is
The bug is an out-of-bounds array access in the D-side pending access tracking logic.

In the `always_comb` block, the code uses:

```systemverilog
pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid
```

This is unsafe when `i == 0`, because `i - 1` becomes `-1`, which is an invalid index for the array. Even though there is a special case for `i == 0` in the first branch, the `else if` still exists in the same conditional chain and can be evaluated in a way that permits the invalid reference.

### 2) Where the problem occurs
The issue occurs in `rtl/ibex_top.sv` inside the `g_dside_tracker` generate block, specifically in the `always_comb` block that builds `pending_dside_accesses_d[i]`.

The problematic section is:

```systemverilog

  if (i == 0 && !pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid) begin
    pending_dside_accesses_d[i].valid = 1'b1;
    pending_dside_accesses_d[i].is_read = ~data_we_o;
  end else if (pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid &
               !pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid) begin
    pending_dside_accesses_d[i].valid = 1'b1;
    pending_dside_accesses_d[i].is_read = ~data_we_o;
  end
end
```

### 3) Best practices to take into account
- Never reference `i - 1` unless `i > 0` is explicitly guaranteed.
- Split boundary cases (`i == 0`) from general cases to make indexing logic safe and obvious.
- Keep the fix minimal and local to the unsafe access.
- Preserve existing behavior for all non-boundary indices.

### 4) How to fix the problem
Refactor the conditional so that:
- the `i == 0` case is handled separately,
- only indices `i > 0` can reach the `i - 1` access,
- the logic remains functionally equivalent.

A safe structure is:

- If `i == 0`, only check whether slot 0 is free and insert there.
- Else, check `pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid` and `!pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid`.

This removes the possibility of out-of-bounds access.

In the `always_comb` block, the code evaluates:

This is unsafe when `i == 0`, because it indexes `-1`, which is out of bounds.

#### 2. Where the problem occurs
The issue is in `rtl/ibex_top.sv` inside the `g_dside_tracker` generate loop, specifically in this conditional branch:

```systemverilog
else if (pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i - 1].valid &
         !pending_dside_accesses_shifted[i].valid) begin
```

Even though there is a special case for `i == 0` earlier in the block, the code still relies on the later branch being unreachable for `i == 0`. The logic should be structured so that the `i == 0` case is explicitly separated and cannot accidentally evaluate `i - 1`.

#### 3. Best practices to take into account
- Avoid array indexing expressions that can underflow, even if guarded indirectly.
- Explicitly separate boundary cases (`i == 0`, last index, etc.) from general cases.
- Prefer clarity over compact conditional logic in hardware generate/always blocks.
- Preserve existing behavior while making the logic structurally safe.

#### 4. How to fix the problem
Refactor the `always_comb` block so that:
- the `i == 0` case is handled separately,
- the `i > 0` case is only evaluated when safe,
- the logic never references `i - 1` unless `i > 0`.

A minimal fix is to restructure the request-grant handling into an explicit `if (i == 0) ... else ...` form, and only use `i - 1` in the `else` branch.

#### 3. Best practices to take into account
- Avoid index arithmetic that can produce invalid indices, especially in hardware description languages where out-of-bounds behavior is unsafe.
- Handle boundary conditions explicitly, particularly for `i == 0`.
- Keep the fix minimal and local to avoid changing intended functionality.
- Preserve the existing access-tracking semantics for all valid entries.

#### 4. How to fix the problem
Refactor the conditional logic so that the `i == 0` case is handled separately from the `i > 0` case.  
For `i == 0`, only allow insertion into slot 0 when it is empty.  
For `i > 0`, keep the existing dependency on the previous slot, but only reference `i - 1` when it is guaranteed to be valid.
